title: make the pane split rule fixed: first split right, every later split down
action: In packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/herding/run.rs the split direction is currently chosen from the parent pane's aspect ratio (fn split_direction(width, height) around line 750: wider-or-square splits right, taller splits down). Live, that keeps sub-dividing width — a 120-column tab goes 60/30/15 and the third worker's pane is unreadable and stalls submissions. The owner wants a FIXED strategy instead: the FIRST split of a tab goes right (one worker gets the full-height column), and EVERY later split goes down, so extra workers stack as full-width horizontal bands ('slides') and width never halves more than once. Change split_direction to take the pane COUNT of the caller's tab instead of a rect: `fn split_direction(pane_count: usize) -> &'static str { if pane_count <= 1 { "right" } else { "down" } }`, and rewrite its doc comment to state the fixed rule and why (readability: a down split leaves width unchanged, so it never trips MIN_PANE_WIDTH). In resolve_split_parent (around line 821) keep the roomiest-pane parent choice unchanged (hps-12) and keep the child-width guard unchanged (hps-13) — only feed the direction from the pane list's len(). The None/empty-layout fallback keeps direction "right" (a tab whose layout cannot be read is treated as its first split). Update the existing unit tests to the new rule: split_direction_prefers_right_when_wider_or_square becomes a count-based test (0 or 1 pane -> right, 2+ -> down); resolve_split_parent_chooses_the_largest_area_pane_even_when_its_child_would_be_too_narrow now has 3 panes so it must expect direction "down", child width 60 unchanged and NO refusal — rename it and rewrite its comment to record that the fixed rule is exactly what removes the old 60/30/15 stall; resolve_split_parent_a_down_split_never_narrows... must supply 2+ panes to reach "down". Keep every other behaviour, comment and test as it is. Do not touch any file outside run.rs.

trace.outcome: split direction is now fixed: right for a tab's first split, down after that; width halves at most once
trace.inline_reason: generation tier here resolves to an external agy cockpit pane; spawning one for a single-file Rust edit costs more than it proves

report.outcome: split_direction now takes the caller tab pane count (<=1 right, else down); resolve_split_parent feeds it from the layout len; hps-12 parent choice and hps-13 child-width guard unchanged; five affected unit tests rewritten to the new rule
report.tests: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee split — green (25 passed) — the split-direction and split-parent decisions are the only behaviour this cell changes; the wider -p bee herding filter also ran, 290 passed with only the pre-existing intentional quick_exit_helper fixture failing
deviations: Executed inline by the orchestrator rather than through a dispatched generation worker (external agy pane tier)
